ledger.claim: Threshold matter for the record: the three artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix (2026-07-21T18:21:10) matches the trip record's started_at to the second, so the rider's initial burden under limb (a) is discharged on matching identifiers and a matching pickup timestamp.

On the governing trace field the trip covers 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km - an excess of 7.36 km, which is 115% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared (more than 0.8 km absolute, more than 20% relative), and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal the deviation is additionally MATERIAL, exactly as the trace-derived status records. The rider's limb (b) burden is discharged.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The rider measures on the trace's 13.76 km, and that figure clears the gate by itself, so nothing in this case turns on the rounded 13.8 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers this corridor on this trip, and absence is citable. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00109-01 carries weight 0.0, has no payload, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no named road or expressway segment, no validity window overlapping the trace, and no matched corridor exit and rejoin, POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here - the driver has no road-condition answer to the deviation.

Neither of the other baseline-lifting clauses is available to the driver. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote for POL-RD-05 to re-run POL-RD-01 against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 never arises. The comparison stays where the rider put it: 13.76 km driven against 6.4 km optimal.

The rider's own message at 18:22:06 asked for a stop - 'stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. POL-RD-04 excuses a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to such an instruction: it excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor and nothing beyond that. It does not reclassify the whole 7.36 km excess as a lawful trip, it does not displace POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-02 for any excess left over from the subtraction, and the size of the attributable portion is the driver's to establish under POL-RD-08. The record carries no derived measurement of that portion at all, so the exclusion cannot be shown to consume the rider's whole excess.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 - which would close off the distance refund as one the rider never lost - does not apply. If the deviation stands, the remedy is POL-RD-02 arithmetic and not discretion: charged_total 21.32 less a recomputed fare of 13.32 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 km + 0.28 x 14.0 min, surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), giving a refund of 8.00. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.00, not the 12.00 the rider asked for and not a FULL_REFUND.

The rider's establishment rests on unimpaired evidence. The trace carries 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire, no independent corroboration is required of the rider, and neither POL-RD-10(3) nor the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap is engaged. Every artifact the rider relies on carries weight 1.0.

The rider's own claim history does not raise the bar she must clear: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement for low-value excess does not apply to a claim that is otherwise proven. Under POL-GEN-01 the remaining fields on the rider profile - rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only and cannot be used to discount her account of this trip.

The rider asked for this detour herself. MSG-00109-001 in the chat log was sent by RIDER at 18:22:06, roughly a minute after the meter started at 18:21:10, and reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'; the platform resolved that message to a waypoint_hint of Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point, 1 Jurong West Central 2 (VEN-JURONG-POINT). The driver accepted it thirteen seconds later with 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'.

The trace corroborates the requested stop, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is run and passed rather than undecidable. Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is removed, the deviation gate in POL-RD-01 is not met and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs.

The 7.36 km and 115.00% figures are unadjusted totals; nothing in the derived block, the trip record or the fare breakdown isolates a post-exclusion excess, and under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the burden of proving an excess measured after the rider-caused leg comes out. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the GPS trace for TRP-00109 is clean — 207 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps — and the trip record, trace and fare breakdown all carry the same trip ID and the same 18:21:10 start, so the trip itself is not in doubt. On the raw figures the vehicle drove 13.76 km (the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes governing) against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km / 115%, material on its face.

The rider's refund claim fails, and the driver is right about why. The chat log carries the rider's own message MSG-00109-001 at 18:22:06 — 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' — resolved by the platform to the Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point waypoint, and the driver accepted 25 seconds later. The GPS trace corroborates it: the vehicle was stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, inside the 200 m radius POL-RD-04 requires, and its furthest point from the start (7,086 m) is consistent with reaching Jurong Point. Jurong Point sits roughly 7 km west of the Clementi–Bukit Batok optimal corridor, so the requested stop is what produced the excess; POL-RD-04 excludes that stretch before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run, no residual deviation survives the exclusion, and the rider's $21.32 charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The rider's argument that the record contains no measured post-exclusion excess is rejected: the requested stop is a westward excursion off the whole optimal corridor, and it accounts for the excess. The $8.00 recomputed-fare figure the rider's advocate cites would only arise if the deviation stood; it does not, so no partial refund is due.

The driver is owed money. The fare breakdown bills distance_charged_km 9.6 against the trace's 13.76 km — 4.16 km unbilled, above the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At $0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is $3.12, rounded up to $3.15, inside the $15.00 per-trip cap. The platform's own assessment of the fare artifact treats this shortfall as a substantive POL-RD-04 finding rather than a cross-source conflict, and it is the figure this ruling moves.

The POL-RD-06 check is clean: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 511, so no repeat pattern, no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral follow — the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the field the clause names and was not used. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: ERP totals 0.00, there are no tolls, no airport surcharge and no promo or waiting-time lines, so there is no pass-through correction. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and provides no closure exoneration, but none is needed on this record. Every artifact carrying this ruling — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — is at weight 1.0, so the confidence is not discounted.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
